How It Works

How Professional Floor Care Works

Our floor care process follows a systematic, six-step protocol designed to maximize pathogen elimination and provide verifiable documentation of results. Every step is performed by trained, background-checked technicians.

1
Floor Assessment

A technician inspects all flooring surfaces to identify type (VCT, carpet, marble, concrete, hardwood), current condition, wear patterns, existing finish layers, and any damage requiring repair before maintenance.

2
Surface Preparation

For hard floors, existing finish is chemically stripped to bare tile using appropriate stripping solution and floor machines. For carpet, pre-treatment solution is applied to break down embedded soil. Furniture is moved and protected.

3
Treatment Application

VCT receives sealer followed by 3-5 coats of commercial-grade floor finish with proper cure time between coats. Carpet receives hot water extraction or encapsulation depending on soil level and drying time requirements. Stone surfaces receive diamond polishing and appropriate sealant.

4
Finish and Cure

Applied products are allowed to cure for the manufacturer-specified duration. VCT finish typically requires 30-60 minutes between coats and 24 hours before heavy traffic. Carpet extraction requires 6-24 hours of drying time with air movers.

5
Quality Inspection

A supervisor inspects all treated surfaces for uniform appearance, proper adhesion, appropriate gloss level, and any defects requiring touch-up. High-traffic areas receive particular attention.

6
Documentation

Before-and-after photos, products used, number of coats applied, and square footage treated are documented in JaniTrack for asset management records and future maintenance scheduling.

FAQ

Floor Care FAQ — Hialeah, FL

Common questions about floor care services in Hialeah.

What is commercial floor care?+
Commercial floor care encompasses the professional maintenance, repair, and refinishing of hard and soft flooring surfaces in commercial environments. It includes VCT stripping and waxing, carpet extraction, marble polishing, concrete sealing, and ongoing maintenance programs. Professional floor care extends floor lifespan by 40-60% compared to neglected floors and maintains the safe, professional appearance that commercial environments require.
How often should commercial floors be stripped and waxed?+
VCT floors in high-traffic areas (lobbies, corridors, cafeterias) should be stripped and refinished every 6-12 months. Moderate-traffic areas typically need annual treatment. Between full strip-and-refinish cycles, quarterly scrub-and-recoat applications and monthly burnishing extend finish life and maintain appearance. Daily dust-mopping is the single most important maintenance practice for VCT longevity.
Do you handle all types of commercial flooring?+
Yes. We service VCT (vinyl composition tile), hardwood, marble, granite, terrazzo, concrete, ceramic tile, luxury vinyl plank, rubber flooring, and all carpet types including broadloom, carpet tile, and area rugs. Each floor type receives specialized treatment using products and equipment specifically designed for that surface. Using incorrect products on flooring surfaces causes damage — which is why professional floor care expertise matters.
Can you restore damaged or neglected floors?+
In most cases, yes. Our restoration services can bring heavily worn VCT with ground-in soil and damaged finish, scratched or etched marble and stone, stained and matted carpet, and deteriorated concrete back to like-new condition. Floor restoration typically costs 60-80% less than replacement and can be completed with minimal disruption to building operations.
What is the difference between buffing, burnishing, and stripping?+
Buffing uses a low-speed floor machine (175-350 RPM) to clean and lightly polish floor finish. Burnishing uses a high-speed machine (1,500-2,500 RPM) to restore gloss through heat and friction without adding new finish. Stripping chemically removes all existing finish down to the bare tile surface, allowing a complete rebuild with fresh sealer and finish coats. Each has a specific place in the floor maintenance lifecycle.
How long does a strip and wax take to complete?+
A typical strip-and-refinish job for a 5,000 sq ft area takes 8-12 hours including stripping, rinsing, sealer application, and 3-5 coats of finish with cure time between coats. The area cannot bear foot traffic for approximately 24 hours after the final coat. We schedule floor work during off-hours, weekends, or building closures to minimize operational disruption.
Do you offer ongoing floor maintenance programs?+
Yes. Our maintenance programs include daily auto-scrubbing for high-traffic hard floors, weekly spray buffing or burnishing, monthly scrub-and-recoat applications, quarterly deep cleaning, and annual or semi-annual strip-and-refinish. Programs are customized based on floor type, traffic patterns, and budget. Scheduled maintenance is significantly more cost-effective than reactive restoration of neglected floors.
